clue.text: Distract the team on the racecourse

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a track is a course for racing

explanation.surface: Someone causes a distraction for a team at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone off their main purpose is to divert their attention, to distract them.

clue.text: American turnover served with his extraordinary Japanese dish

indicators.note: a turnover flips the abbreviation over so it reads backwards
extraordinary signals that the letters of his are put out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: An American pastry is served alongside an unusual dish from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American turnover' reads like a pastry from the US, but 'turnover' flips the abbreviation, and 'extraordinary' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegared rice with raw fish is a classic food from Japan.

clue.text: Small thick pancake falls on ice cream container

parts.note: drops means falls
a cone is the wafer holder for ice cream

explanation.surface: A pancake tumbles on to an ice cream cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish pancake made by dropping batter on a griddle is exactly this small, thick sort.

clue.text: Square-rigger's mast might be better on Valiant

parts.note: to top something is to better it
gallant means valiant, brave

explanation.surface: A mast on a sailing ship might be improved on a vessel called Valiant.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged sailing ship, this is the mast section above the topmast.

clue.text: A non-drinker almost drained by the effort

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: almost means the word is stopped short of its final letter

parts.note: empty means drained

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is nearly exhausted by the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of EMPTY to leave EMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try, an endeavour or effort.

clue.text: Kipling's hero soon changed Japanese garment

definitions.note: the clue's definition is singular while the entry is plural

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of soon are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Kipling's boy hero quickly switches into Japanese clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges SOON to ONOS. The grid gives the plural though the definition is singular.
explanation.definitionFit: These long wide-sleeved robes are the traditional dress of Japan.

clue.text: Elected official shot on the billiard table

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
off. is a standard abbreviation for official

explanation.surface: A newly elected official is shot dead over a billiard table.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards and snooker, an in-off is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket after striking another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards stroke where the cue ball is pocketed off an object ball has this name.

clue.text: Muslim country administered by leader of imams

indicators.note: leader of points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: ran means administered, managed

explanation.surface: An Islamic state is governed by its chief clerics.
explanation.definitionFit: This Middle Eastern nation is an Islamic republic.

clue.text: Bulb is working with current on

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
I is the symbol for electric current
taken as written

explanation.surface: A light bulb is switched on, with power flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light bulb, but it is the vegetable. I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable grows as a layered bulb underground.

clue.text: Stupid parent almost dead drunk

indicators.note: almost cuts the word short by its final letter

parts.note: a father is a parent

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of dead reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish dad is almost passed out from drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FATHER to FATHE; 'drunk' turns DEAD into ADED.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is an idiot, so to be like one is to be dim-witted.

clue.text: Exclusive small shop

parts.note: a co-op is a cooperative store

explanation.surface: A tiny shop sells only exclusive goods.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism, a story one paper gets before its rivals is a scoop, an exclusive.

clue.text: Pat isn't my original drummer

indicators.note: original suggests a fresh, inventive arrangement of the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone insists Pat was not their first drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges the letters of PAT ISN'T MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of kettledrums in an orchestra is a percussionist who drums.

clue.text: Put me on National Trust section of programme

parts.note: to instal is to put in place
taken as written
NT is short for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be put on a National Trust segment of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: INSTAL is the British spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: One episode in a serial is a single part delivered in a series.

clue.text: Genuflect without using left leg joint

indicators.note: without using means a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to kneel is to genuflect

explanation.surface: Someone bows down without bending their left leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between thigh and shin is the main joint of the leg.

clue.text: Agile housebreaker who nicks one's kit?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicks' is British slang for steals; a kit is a young cat, so one who steals a cat's young is literally a cat-burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who climbs nimbly into buildings; read literally, a robber of a cat's offspring.

clue.text: Sink has allowed for very small amount of liquid

parts.note: to drop is to sink
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A sink has been allowed to hold only a little water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny drop is a minute quantity of fluid.

clue.text: After last month the Speaker can represent a painter

indicators.note: after places one piece following the other, so the speaker comes behind the month

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month of the year
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: After December, the Speaker of Parliament may stand in for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the parliamentary Speaker, but any orator will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and decorator does up rooms, so a painter is one kind of decorator.

clue.text: Main drug derived from algae

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
weed is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A principal drug is extracted from pond scum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' as the sea is a poetic usage common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine plants such as kelp are large algae.

clue.text: Protocol is quite wrong better not to take sides

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of quite are arranged incorrectly
the sides of a word are its first and last letters, which are dropped

explanation.surface: Breaking protocol is quite wrong; it is better to stay neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges QUITE to ETIQU; 'not to take sides' removes the first and last letters of BETTER, leaving ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal rules of polite behaviour are a code of correct conduct.

clue.text: Char's beginning to consume less fat

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: leaner means having less fat

explanation.surface: A fish starts to eat less fatty food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like the fish or burning, but a char is a British charwoman, a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A char, short for charwoman, is a woman hired to do housework.

clue.text: A gathering of friends in the Indian Ocean

explanation.surface: Old friends meet up on an island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the island Réunion, a French territory in the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-together of old acquaintances; also a French island east of Madagascar.

clue.text: Put up again, recharged so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to be rebilled is to be charged again

explanation.surface: A rebuilt structure means customers are charged again, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct something a second time is to erect it anew.

clue.text: Military bridge builders negotiate withdrawal

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps that builds bridges
to treat is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Army engineers negotiate a pull-back.
explanation.definitionFit: An army's pull-back from the enemy is a military retreat.

clue.text: OT wife's humdrum existence with husband

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unvarying routine

explanation.surface: An Old Testament wife lives a dull life with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: OT is the Old Testament; Ruth married Boaz in the Book of Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moabite heroine of the Book of Ruth was the wife of Boaz.

clue.text: Savour old dance

parts.note: a tang is a sharp savour or flavour

explanation.surface: Someone relishes an old-fashioned dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argentine ballroom dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Rehearsal when continuous sequence of performances has finished?

parts.note: a run is a show's series of performances
through means finished, done

explanation.surface: A rehearsal held only after the show's run is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RUN + THROUGH, the phrase is a run that is finished; the question mark marks that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance of a whole piece is a full rehearsal.

clue.text: Husband with an unoccupied day could be useful

indicators.note: unoccupied means the word is emptied of its middle, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A husband with a free day might be helpful around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient and practical to have about is of use.

clue.text: Only 80% of island whisky shows in normal trade statistics

definitions.note: the core sense is whisky; the words before it point to four of the five letters of Malta, the Mediterranean island

indicators.note: shows in says the word is on display within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Only a fraction of the island's whisky turns up in the usual trade figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition carries its own cryptic support: 80% of MALTA, four letters of five, is the same word. 'statistics' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is whisky distilled from malted barley, and an island malt is one from Scotland's isles.

clue.text: Make frustrated Latins eat out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Latin people dining out cause annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LATINS EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease with something desirable kept just out of reach is to frustrate, after the mythical Tantalus.

clue.text: Reveal it's left the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone discloses that they have left the school.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge a secret is to disclose it.

clue.text: Rubbish — inside there's very large area for sleeping birds

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense
OS is short for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Within the rubbish there is a large patch where birds sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: OS, for outsize, is a clothing-size label meaning very large; 'there's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle for the night.

clue.text: Move to orient year after scandal

indicators.note: after places the year abbreviation behind the rearranged letters
move signals that the letters of the words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone moves east for a year after a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges TO ORIENT to NOTORIET; Y follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy or ill fame is the state that a scandal brings.
